newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court adjourns talks on Telekom sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court adjourns talks on Telekom sell-off.

text.p: Turkey's constitutional court on Wednesday adjourned a hearing on whether to approve the sale of Turk Telekom, the centrepiece of the government's privatisation plans.
Court chairman Yekta Gungor Ozden told reporters at the end of the afternoon session that talks would resume on Thursday morning.
The Islamist-led government hopes to raise $3.5 billion from the state telecommunications company' sale, which has already been halted three times by the court since 1993.
The court is currently ruling on a fresh request by mainly leftist opposition MPs to block the sell-off again.
The first tranche of up to 15 percent of Telekom is to be sold by the end of the year if the court gives the green light, privatisation officials say.

Recent sales of a bank and tyre and cement factories and the leasing of port facilities have boosted the government's hopes of reaching a target of $5 billion from sell-offs this year. That figure does not include any revenues from Telekom.
